title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is witnessing a mix of strategic partnerships and regulatory shifts, with Northrop Grumman and Apex teaming up on interceptors while spaceport facility bonds become law. Meanwhile, China's launch activities continue unabated, and the launch market feels the strain from recent setbacks.

themes.title: Partnerships in Space Defense
themes.body: Northrop Grumman's collaboration with Apex on space-based interceptors signals a growing emphasis on defensive capabilities in orbit. This trend is likely to attract further partnerships as nations prioritize space security.

themes.title: Regulatory Changes Ahead
themes.body: The recent passage of spaceport facility bonds could reshape how space infrastructure is financed, potentially unlocking new investment avenues. This legislative shift may also encourage more private players to enter the market.

themes.title: China's Launch Surge
themes.body: China's unexpected launch of the Long March 12B, coupled with its test of direct-to-device satellites, underscores its aggressive push in space capabilities. Such developments may heighten competitive tensions in the global space race.

themes.title: Launch Market Woes
themes.body: The failure of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket adds to the ongoing challenges facing the launch market, which is already grappling with capacity constraints. Stakeholders will need to reassess timelines and strategies as reliability issues persist.
